expectationsBeforeClassifierEdit: Gross imports and gross exports are separate activities. Net imports (imports minus exports) are out of the fixed activity vocabulary, not an alternative import total.

Full crude-and-petroleum-products totals can represent whole petroleum. Individual fuels, finished-products-only, grades, bonded status, SPR-only and excluding-SPR flows are narrower. Crude and gasoline remain explicit qualifiers, never whole petroleum.
EIA total motor gasoline includes finished motor gasoline and blending components in trade; finished gasoline and blending components alone remain narrower when a broader total exists.
Country names in U.S. imports-from and exports-to are partners. Whole U.S. trade requires all partners, not one country or group. Never interpret a partner code as that country total.
Import area of entry is not destination consumption; PADD/refining districts never become states. State residual-fuel import series remain petroleum components.

Rail receipts from within the U.S. are domestic movements, not imports, sales, production or consumption. Cross-border Canada/US rail movements are transport-mode components of trade, never all-modal totals.
Preserve EIA territorial scope: trade into/out of 50 states and DC includes Puerto Rico, Virgin Islands and other possessions as partners.
Weekly export values are estimates; label that source basis. Earlier restrictive legal wording in a weekly note is historical, not a present routing or eligibility rule.
Original codes/names/frequencies/call references are preserved. Unknown or contradictory metadata remains pending. Missing units remain ineligible, never guessed.
No summing countries, fuels or modal components to invent unpublished totals.

findings.finding: Weekly total gasoline includes finished gasoline and blending components. Weekly exports are estimates; contemporary monthly notes supersede old export-restriction wording.
Imports count bonded quantities upon withdrawal under stated customs conditions; bonded and non-bonded series are components.
Residual-fuel state imports are a fuel component, not whole petroleum; U.S. scope is 50 states plus DC.
Export subject is U.S.; foreign and territorial names identify destinations, not their own total exports.
Net imports are a balance rather than gross imports; some component balances use assumed zero exports.
Imports include SPR and are reported by PADD entry; named foreign origin does not become requested-country total.
Rail data are EIA estimates using Surface Transportation Board and other information; cover domestic and Canada cross-border movements.
Rail table explicitly separates intra-U.S. movements, U.S. exports to Canada and U.S. imports from Canada.

scopeCasesForCheckpoint.decision: Only all-partner totals qualify for whole subject trade. Regional/bilateral/modal flows remain components; net trade stays outside fixed activities.
Keep official weekly estimates with explicit basis label and compare compatible monthly/annual source totals before default selection.
EIA total includes blending components; finished-only and blendstock-only remain product components; no invented sum.
